newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries trade in London peters out quietly.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries trade in London peters out quietly.

text.p: Trade in U.S. Treasuries in London petered out in typical end-of-year fashion on Tuesday with scant buying or selling interest.
At 1108 GMT, the 30-year bond was at 99-14/32 to yield 6.543 percent, against 99-19/32 in Tokyo and 99-16/32 in New York.
March T-bond futures were at 113-30/32, up 2/32.
"Zip is happening. Nothing is trading," said one trader with a French bank in London.
"The only activity is maintenance trades by central banks doing repo stuff and switching in and out of various issues. It is just a case of cleaning up books," he said.
The trader said the outlook was fairly positive for Treasuries in early 1997, but holiday concerns were uppermost in traders' minds for the moment.
U.S. new home sales data for November due at 1500 GMT was unlikely to generate much interest because "no one will be here to trade it".
